Assemble the lateral launch surveys and rank the laterals by defect severity and backup history
Confirm the public and private boundary rule for the street and list what each owner must arrange on their portion

Confirm each manhole dimensions, depth, pipe entries, and infiltration points from the pre rehabilitation assessments
Record each completed manhole with photos and update its condition grade and next inspection date in the asset system
Plan flow control for each structure, including plugs or bypass where live infiltration would wash out the lining
Schedule the structures in an order that keeps a working access route and completes the worst infiltration first

Confirm the leaking joints and their chainages from the CCTV and wet weather records and group them into grouting setups
File the grouting record by chainage and schedule a wet weather recheck to confirm the infiltration reduction
Confirm the groundwater and flow conditions suit grouting and plan the work for the season when leaks are active but flows are manageable
Retest each sealed joint and note any joint that still leaks for the follow up method decision
Set up each joint with the packer, test the joint by pressure as directed, and record the test result before injecting

tasks.explanation: Grouting is a joint by joint repair, so each joint is tested before and after injection and its grout take is recorded. Joints that refuse to seal are not hidden in the total; they move to the next method decision with evidence.

Record the bypass log during the job and confirm normal flow is restored and plugs removed before demobilizing
Set the watch schedule, fuel plan, alarm hookups, and the spill kit and containment placement for the full bypass period
Calculate the bypass capacity from the recorded peak flow in the job file and add the standby pump so firm capacity exceeds the peak
Plan the suction and discharge manholes, including plugs, sandbag or bladder sealing, and surcharge monitoring upstream
Test run the bypass at full flow before the work starts and confirm upstream levels stay below the surcharge trigger

tasks.explanation: Bypass firm capacity must exceed the recorded peak with a pump failed, not just on paper. A full flow test before the pipe is opened proves the plan, and the watch, fuel, and spill arrangements cover the hours when nobody is watching by default.

Verify the measurement rules in the draft tender match how each item will be measured on site

List all projects with warranty end dates in the next quarter from the contract register
Schedule acceptance style CCTV and manhole inspections early enough that deficiencies can be corrected inside the warranty

Assemble the blockage history, the graded CCTV, and the cleaning costs for the section over the last five years
Enter the selected project in the capital plan with its evidence file and set the interim cleaning interval until construction
Confirm whether the pipe alignment, grade, and capacity are adequate, since lining keeps all three unchanged
Check whether spot repairs plus root control could safely defer capital work past the repaving window, and state the risk

Complete the entry permit and hazard assessment, naming the entrants, attendant, and supervisor for this entry
Exit, account for all entrants and tools, restore the pumps, prove the new float on a real cycle, and close the permit
Isolate and lock out both pumps and any inflow control that could change the well level during entry
Enter and complete the float replacement while the attendant logs atmosphere retests at the permit intervals
Set up ventilation and run it long enough to clear the space, then test the atmosphere at top, middle, and bottom before entry

tasks.explanation: The permit, isolation, and rescue arrangements exist before anyone enters, because wet well hazards develop faster than an improvised rescue. Atmosphere is tested at all levels since gases stratify, and the entry closes only after the station is proven back in service.

Fully calibrate any detector that fails or responds slowly and repeat the bump test after calibration
Remove from service and tag any detector that still fails and issue a verified spare to the affected crew

tasks.explanation: A bump test proves the sensors still respond, which is the failure that matters in the field. Results are recorded by serial number so a faulty unit cannot quietly return to a truck, and gas stock is managed so testing is never skipped for lack of supplies.

Keep ventilation running for the whole entry and retest at the permit intervals and after any break in ventilation
Complete the permit and confirm the blower capacity suits the space volume and the duct length to the bottom
Stop the entry and ventilate again if any reading moves toward its limit, and record the event on the permit
Position the blower upwind of the opening with its intake clear of vehicle exhaust and generator fumes
Test the atmosphere at top, middle, and bottom with ventilation running and confirm results stay within entry limits

Keep the system rigged and attended for the full entry, including breaks when the entrant stays in the space
Attach the entrant harness and winch line and complete a controlled lift check with the entrant just clear of the ladder

tasks.explanation: Retrieval is rigged and lift checked before entry, because a system assembled during an emergency is too slow. The attendant, not a rescue team, is the first rescue, and the equipment stays rigged whenever anyone is in the space.

File the updated inventory with the program review date and the name of the person who completed the assessments
Update the space signs and the inventory database and remove spaces that no longer exist or are no longer confined
List all spaces from the asset register and add the new capital project spaces with their locations and access details
Classify each space under the program categories and record whether entry is permit required and what isolations apply
Brief the crews and contractors who use the inventory on the changes and the new assessments

Hold a pre job meeting covering station hazards, utility isolations, communication, and who may authorize the entry
Confirm the contractor atmosphere testing and ventilation are in place and review the first test results together before entry

Confirm the contractor entry program, training records, and rescue arrangements meet the utility requirements before the date is set

tasks.prompt: Order the atmospheric testing sequence during an ongoing wet well entry.

Order the entrant out at once if any reading reaches its action limit and record the reading and time on the permit
Ventilate and retest until readings are stable within limits before any re entry is authorized by the supervisor
Repeat testing at the permit intervals and whenever inflow rate, ventilation, or the work activity changes
Test oxygen first, then flammable gases, then the toxic gases listed on the permit, using the calibrated detector
Lower the sampling probe to the entrant working level and test at that level, not only at the opening

tasks.explanation: Test order matters because oxygen content affects the other readings. Testing happens at the working level where the entrant breathes, trends are kept for the hazard assessment, and a limit reading ends the entry without negotiation.

tasks.prompt: Order the confined space program review after a near miss gas alarm event.

Issue corrective actions, such as ventilation changes, retraining, or equipment replacement, each with an owner and a date
Secure the detector and download its logged readings and confirm the alarm value and duration from the record, not from memory
Share the lessons at all crew toolbox talks and file the review in the safety program record with the follow up check date
Interview the entrant, attendant, and supervisor separately about the setup, ventilation, and testing that preceded the alarm
Check whether the same gaps appear in other recent permits or at other sites in the program

tasks.explanation: The detector log gives facts before opinions are collected, and separate interviews keep accounts honest. Corrective actions are checked for the same gaps elsewhere, because a near miss usually reveals a program weakness, not one crew error.

tasks.prompt: Order the coordination of a sanitary sewer overflow response at a blocked collector.

Confirm the report location and extent, notify the supervisor, and dispatch the first crew to protect the overflow point
Complete the follow up report, including any CCTV or repair work order raised to prevent a repeat at the same location
Stop or reduce the overflow by jetting the blockage or setting bypass pumping, containing the flow with sandbags or berms at the ditch
Record volumes estimated, duration, cause found, and the notifications made with times in the spill record
Notify the required provincial contact and downstream users as directed by the spill procedure once the overflow is confirmed

tasks.explanation: Protection and containment start before the cause is known, because every minute of overflow adds volume. Notifications follow confirmation so reports are factual, and the record closes with prevention work, not just cleanup.

tasks.prompt: Order the response coordination for a cluster of basement backups on one street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Recheck each affected home or advise residents to run water and confirm their services now drain, recording who confirmed
Log each address and time, advise residents to limit water use, and notify the supervisor of a probable mainline blockage
Jet the blocked reach from downstream with vacuum capture and confirm the surcharge level falls in the upstream manhole
Arrange cleanup guidance information for affected residents as directed by the utility procedure and log what was provided

tasks.explanation: A dry weather cluster is treated as a mainline event from the first call, which gets the right crew moving sooner. Homes are rechecked individually because a falling manhole level does not prove every lateral cleared, and an unexplained cause earns a camera run.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a force main break discharging near a roadway.

cards.label: Complete the repair or install a temporary bypass, disinfect the repair, and return the main to service with a controlled pressure test
Notify the required provincial contact and the roads group and record the notification times in the event log
Set traffic control and contain the discharge with berms and the vacuum truck, keeping sewage out of the storm ditch
Excavate to expose the break once locates are complete and confirm the pipe material, size, and failure type
Clean and disinfect the affected area, estimate the spilled volume, and file the break report with the repair record
Stop the lift station pumps or close the station discharge to halt the flow to the break and notify the supervisor at once

tasks.explanation: Stopping the pumps is the spill control, because a force main break discharges at pump pressure until the station stops. Containment and notification run in parallel, and the main returns to service only after a controlled test so the repair is proven before full duty.

tasks.prompt: Order a lift station overflow response where bypass pumping is needed.

tasks.configuration: Scope: both pumps have failed during a storm, the wet well is overflowing, and portable pumps and tankers are on route.

cards.label: Clean and disinfect the overflow area, estimate the total volume, and complete the spill report with the repair follow up
Rotate tanker hauling to the receiving station if bypass capacity cannot match the inflow and log the volumes hauled
Restore the station pumps or keep the bypass running until repairs are complete and the level is controlled through a full cycle
Set the portable bypass pump with suction in the wet well and discharge to the downstream manhole or force main connection
Confirm the overflow start time and extent, notify the supervisor, and set containment at the overflow point
Make the required provincial notification with the estimated rate and the receiving area as directed by the procedure

tasks.explanation: Containment and notification come before repair because the overflow is the environmental event. Bypass is sized to the inflow, tankers cover the gap honestly with logged volumes, and the event closes only when the station controls its level unaided.

tasks.prompt: Order spill containment where an overflow is moving toward a creek crossing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow from a surcharged manhole is flowing overland about 100 m from a creek in a park area.

cards.label: Stop the source by clearing the blockage or bypassing the surcharged reach while containment crews hold the line
Vacuum all pooled sewage from the overland path and wash down and disinfect the affected ground as directed
Dispatch the first crew directly to the creek edge to place containment before working at the manhole

Confirm the panel backup battery carries the controls and alarm dialer on a brief power interruption test

tasks.prompt: Two similar housing basins in a Saskatchewan city are flow monitored for a spring month, and one basin shows far higher night flow than the other.

Groundwater infiltration through pipe and joint defects in Basin A, where groundwater sits above the pipes

A faulty flow meter in Basin A reading about three times too high

nextClue.prompt: Which follow up best locates the entry points in Basin A?

CCTV during high groundwater with infiltration noted at each joint, paired with the groundwater level log

clueText.nc-a: Billing already showed equal night use, so a survey cannot explain a threefold flow gap.
clueText.nc-b: The high flow persisted through a dry spell, so rainfall records cannot locate dry weather entry points.
clueText.nc-c: Camera runs show several joints in Basin A weeping steadily while groundwater is high, and dry joints where groundwater is low.

tasks.prompt: A Manitoba trunk sewer is monitored through summer storms, and its flow jumps within half an hour of heavy rain and falls back within two hours.

Fast rainfall dependent inflow from direct storm connections, rather than groundwater infiltration
A treatment plant recycle stream discharged to the trunk during storms

nextClue.prompt: Which test best hunts the direct connections?

A year of monthly groundwater well readings
A census review of population change

nextClue.explanation: Smoke and dye testing directly reveal storm connections to the sanitary sewer.

clueText.nc-a: Smoke appears at several roof leaders and one catch basin, and dye from a roof leader reaches the sanitary manhole in minutes.
clueText.nc-b: Groundwater is already known to sit below the inverts, so more well readings cannot explain the storm spikes.
clueText.nc-c: Population change is gradual and cannot produce a 30 minute spike that clears in two hours.

The paired before and after night flow comparison for the sealed and control basins, with the manhole leak inspection notes

tasks.prompt: A permanent flow meter on an Alberta trunk reads 30 percent higher than a portable meter installed beside it for a month.

A bench calibration test of the permanent meter shows a steady positive drift across the test range.
Sewer flow conditions and contributing population do not change during the month.

options.label: The trunk truly carries 30 percent more flow than the pump station receives
The permanent meter has drifted out of calibration and is overstating flow by about 30 percent
The portable meter is under reading because of where it was installed
Growth in the catchment added 30 percent more flow that month

inference.explanation: Two independent checks agree with the portable meter, cleaning changes nothing, and bench testing shows steady drift. The permanent record, not the flow, is wrong, which matters before any I/I program is sized from it.

options.label: Correct the historical record using the bench calibration result and schedule routine meter verification
Size the I/I rehabilitation program from the permanent meter record as it stands
Remove the portable meter and rely on the permanent meter alone

nextClue.explanation: Correcting the data and verifying meters routinely keeps program decisions on true flows.

clueText.nc-a: Bench results give a consistent correction across the range, and a verification schedule is added to the monitoring plan.
clueText.nc-b: Sizing a program from a record known to read 30 percent high would overspend on capacity that does not exist.
clueText.nc-c: Removing the check meter leaves the drifted instrument as the only source again.

A general statement that foundation drains are often connected

clueText.nc-b: The file pairs a positive smoke result and a 10 minute dye transfer at that address with a sound main.
clueText.nc-c: A general statement does not prove this property is connected.

tasks.prompt: Flows in a riverside Saskatchewan basin rise and fall with river level over several days, even in dry weather.

A basement flooding complaint count for one street
Basin flow plotted against river level and rainfall together over a full season

clueText.nc-b: Complaint counts locate impacts, not the water entry mechanism.
clueText.nc-c: Across the season, flow tracks river level with a one day lag and shows no response to several moderate rains.

tasks.prompt: Night flow in an industrial basin in Edmonton spikes at 2 a.m. on weekdays, and the first suspicion is infiltration.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian flow monitoring study. Flows, rainfall and levels are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The spike occurs only on weekday nights and never on weekends or holidays.

A drinking water main leak entering the sewer on weekday nights

clueText.nc-b: Lining sound, tight pipes would spend the I/I budget on a discharge that is not infiltration.

tasks.prompt: A lined basin and an unlined control basin in a Manitoba city are monitored through the same storms before and after lining.

Lining reduced the basin dry weather sanitary flow

Before and after storm response for treated and control basins at matched rainfall, stated as percent of dry weather flow
The total liner length installed, with no flow result

clueText.nc-b: The summary shows the treated basin storm peak falling from about 300 percent to about 140 percent of dry weather flow at matched rainfall.

tasks.prompt: An old clay pipe basin in Winnipeg has very high night flow but only a modest flow rise during storms.

evidence.label: Minimum night flow is about three times the value expected from night water use.
Storm responses are small and slow, building over a day rather than minutes.
Groundwater stands above the pipe inverts for most of the year in this basin.

Basins with newer gasketed pipe in the same city show low night flow under the same groundwater.

Chronic groundwater infiltration through the many clay pipe joints dominates this basin, more than storm inflow
A large water main leak feeds the sewer every night

options.label: A roof leader disconnection program as the first and main measure
Replacing the flow meter with a larger unit
Joint sealing and pipe renewal in the high groundwater reaches, prioritised by CCTV infiltration severity

nextClue.explanation: Matching the remedy to chronic joint infiltration targets the water that is actually entering.

clueText.nc-b: Meter size does not explain trickles seen entering at joints on camera.
clueText.nc-c: The plan ranks reaches by camera observed infiltration under high groundwater and schedules sealing and renewal there first.

tasks.prompt: A bypass pumping plan for a planned station shutdown in a prairie city is checked against the station flows before the work is approved.

Wet weather will not occur during the planned week
The creek beside the station makes a short overflow acceptable

nextClue.explanation: A capacity and standby condition turns the flow record into a clear approval test.

clueText.nc-b: Working faster does not add pumping capacity during a storm peak.

Dye placed in the catch basin appears in the sanitary manhole shortly after.
The catch basin and sanitary manhole are the only structures showing smoke on the street.
CCTV of the sanitary main between them shows no break or open joint.
Dry weather flow in the sanitary sewer rises quickly when the catch basin receives hose water.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Smoke leaked through the soil from a broken sanitary pipe
The catch basin is correctly connected to the storm sewer only
Wind blew sanitary smoke across the street into the catch basin grate
The catch basin is cross connected to the sanitary sewer below ground

inference.explanation: Dye and hose water both move from the catch basin into the sanitary sewer, and the main is sound, so a direct cross connection exists. Wind cannot move dye or hose water.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the repair order for the cross connection?

options.label: The dye transfer timing plus a camera run from the catch basin lead showing it joining the sanitary pipe
A photograph of smoke at the grate alone
A wind record for the test day

nextClue.explanation: A camera run showing the physical connection is the direct proof a repair crew needs.

clueText.nc-a: The lead camera shows the catch basin pipe joining the sanitary main, matching the dye timing.
clueText.nc-b: Smoke at a grate can have other causes, so a photo alone is weaker than the connection itself.
clueText.nc-c: Wind records cannot explain dye moving between the systems.

tasks.prompt: Smoke testing in a Calgary neighbourhood brings smoke into one home through a basement floor drain, and residents fear a broken sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Smoke enters only at the floor drain and at no plumbing fixture with a filled trap.
The floor drain trap is found dry, with its trap primer line shut off.
CCTV of the home lateral and the main shows both sound with no defects.
No smoke appears at the ground surface or at neighbouring homes.
After the trap is filled with water, a repeat smoke test produces no smoke in the home.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Smoke entered through the dry floor drain trap, not through a sewer defect
The home lateral is cracked under the basement floor
The main sewer is pressurising the home plumbing
Smoke came through a foundation crack from a leaking main

inference.explanation: A dry trap, sound pipes on camera, and a clean repeat test after filling the trap isolate the trap as the pathway. A cracked lateral would still admit smoke after the trap was filled.

nextClue.prompt: Which follow up best prevents a repeat at this home?

options.label: Excavate and replace the home lateral
Restore the trap primer supply and confirm the trap holds water at a follow up visit
Lower the smoke test pressure for the whole street

nextClue.explanation: Keeping the trap filled addresses the actual pathway found.

clueText.nc-a: Replacing a lateral that camera showed sound would not fix a dry trap.
clueText.nc-b: The primer line is reopened and the trap is holding water at the follow up check.
clueText.nc-c: Test pressure was normal, and other homes with filled traps had no smoke.

tasks.prompt: A roof leader dye test in a British Columbia town puts green dye into one downspout, and the dye shows up in the sanitary sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Dye appears in the sanitary manhole 8 minutes after it is poured into the downspout.
No dye appears in the storm manhole on the same street during the test.
The same test at three neighbouring homes sends dye to the storm sewer only.
Flow in the sanitary sewer rises during rain at this street, matching the test result.
The home was built when combined connections were being phased out in the area.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The dye leaked through soil from the storm pipe into the sanitary pipe
This home roof leader is connected to the sanitary sewer and adds storm inflow
All homes on the street drain their roofs to the sanitary sewer
The storm sewer was blocked, so dye backed up into the sanitary sewer

inference.explanation: Dye reached sanitary but not storm, neighbours tested correctly to storm, and the street sanitary flow responds to rain. That is a property specific sanitary roof connection.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best completes the file for this property?

options.label: Assume every home on the street needs the same disconnection order without testing
Test the storm sewer capacity instead
Repeat dye confirmation with a flow timed observation at the sanitary manhole and a dated test record for the address

nextClue.explanation: A dated, address specific confirmed result is what a disconnection file needs.

clueText.nc-a: Neighbours tested to the storm sewer, so street wide orders without testing would be wrong.
clueText.nc-b: Storm capacity does not change where this roof drains.
clueText.nc-c: The repeat test confirms an 8 minute dye arrival at the sanitary manhole and is filed for that address.

tasks.prompt: Smoke testing a Saskatchewan street finds smoke rising from one backyard cleanout cap that is cracked, and nowhere else on the property.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Smoke rises steadily from the cracked cleanout cap in the backyard.
No smoke appears at the home roof vent beyond the normal vent discharge, at fixtures, or at the ground over the lateral.
Dye flushed in the home reaches the main normally with no surface dye.
CCTV from the cleanout shows the lateral sound to the main.
Replacing the cap and repeating the test produces no smoke escape at the property.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lateral is broken under the backyard and venting smoke
The main sewer has a defect at this connection
The cracked cleanout cap was the only smoke escape and the lateral itself is sound
The home plumbing vents are blocked and forcing smoke out

inference.explanation: Smoke at one cracked cap, a sound lateral on camera, normal dye travel, and a clean retest after a cap replacement isolate a minor surface defect, not a pipe failure.

nextClue.prompt: Which disposition best fits this finding in the source detection program?

options.label: Record it as a minor private side defect corrected on site, not as a main or lateral failure
Schedule the lateral for lining because of the smoke result
Add the main reach for excavation and replacement

nextClue.explanation: Recording the true scale of the defect keeps program resources on real sources.

clueText.nc-a: The file records a cracked cap replaced and a clean retest, with the lateral noted sound on camera.
clueText.nc-b: Lining a sound lateral spends rehabilitation money where no defect exists.
clueText.nc-c: The main showed no defect at this connection, so excavation is not supported.

tasks.prompt: A basin in Alberta still shows a strong storm flow response after the mains were lined and manholes sealed, and crews turn to the private side.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Post lining storm response in the basin is nearly unchanged from before lining.
Smoke testing finds smoke at many lateral joints in rear yards across the basin.
CCTV of the lined mains shows a sound, sealed pipe with no infiltration.
Dye tests confirm several laterals carry storm water quickly to the main during hose tests.
Basins where laterals were also renewed show a large storm response drop in the same program.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The liner has failed throughout the basin and is leaking at every joint
Manholes are still the main entry route after sealing
The flow meters drifted after lining and invented the storm response
Private laterals are the remaining major inflow and infiltration route in this basin

inference.explanation: Sound lined mains, unchanged response, smoke at many lateral joints, and better results where laterals were renewed point to the private side as the remaining route.

nextClue.prompt: Which program step best follows from this evidence?

options.label: Re-line the mains a second time
Add a lateral inspection and renewal stream to the basin program, using the smoke and dye results to rank properties
Remove the basin flow meters

nextClue.explanation: Targeting the laterals addresses the route the evidence identifies.

clueText.nc-a: Re-lining a sound main does not reach water entering through laterals.
clueText.nc-b: The program adds lateral camera inspections ranked by the smoke and dye findings for the basin.
clueText.nc-c: Removing meters hides the response instead of fixing its source.

tasks.prompt: Dry weather flow appears at a storm outfall in a Manitoba town, and sanitary dye testing is used to check for a sanitary source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: The storm outfall runs steadily in dry weather with a sewage like odour.
Dye placed in a sanitary manhole upstream appears at the storm outfall within the hour.
A camera run in the storm pipe finds a sanitary lateral crossing into it at one address.
Rain has not fallen for six days before the observation.
Other storm outfalls in town are dry in the same period.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A sanitary lateral is cross connected into the storm pipe and discharging in dry weather
Groundwater is entering the storm pipe along its whole length
A drinking water main leak is feeding the storm outfall
Storm pipe sediment is releasing stored rain water slowly

inference.explanation: Dye transfer, a camera found cross connection, dry weather, and other dry outfalls identify a sanitary cross connection rather than groundwater or stored rain.

nextClue.prompt: Which action best fits the finding under general provincial wastewater requirements?

options.label: Wait for the next rain to dilute the outfall flow
Add the outfall to a list for review next year
Isolate and repair the cross connection, and document the dry weather discharge and its correction

nextClue.explanation: A dry weather sanitary discharge to a storm outfall calls for prompt repair and documentation.

clueText.nc-a: Dilution does not correct a continuous sanitary discharge.
clueText.nc-b: Leaving a known cross connection for a year prolongs an unpermitted style discharge.
clueText.nc-c: The lateral is reconnected to the sanitary sewer and the outfall runs dry at the follow up check.

tasks.prompt: A first smoke test on a windy day in a coastal town finds almost no defects, but the basin flow data says inflow sources must exist.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Wind gusts on the test day repeatedly blew smoke sideways and thinned it at vents.
Basin flow monitoring shows a strong, fast storm response.
A repeat test on a calm morning finds smoke at four roof leaders and two yard drains.
Crews and equipment, test pressure and plugging were the same on both days.
Dye tests confirm two of the calm day findings reach the sanitary sewer.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The basin has no inflow sources and the flow data is wrong
The windy first test was unreliable and missed sources that the calm retest found
The sources appeared between the two test days because of new construction
Smoke testing cannot work in this town at all

inference.explanation: Same crews and setup, a strong flow signal, and confirmed finds on the calm day show weather invalidated the first pass. The method worked when conditions allowed.

nextClue.prompt: Which program rule best follows from this pair of tests?

options.label: Set weather limits for smoke testing and retest basins tested in high wind before reporting them clear
Report the first test result and close the basin
Abandon smoke testing in favour of flow monitoring alone

nextClue.explanation: A weather limit with retesting protects the program from false clear results.

clueText.nc-a: The program sets a wind limit and lists the windy day basin for retest before any clear report.
clueText.nc-b: Closing the basin on a test known to be compromised would leave real sources in place.
clueText.nc-c: Flow monitoring shows a problem exists but cannot locate the connections smoke testing finds.

tasks.prompt: Smoke rises from cracks in a low ditch along a rural Alberta road during testing of the sanitary sewer in the ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Smoke rises at several ground cracks along the ditch line above the sewer.
Excavation at one crack finds a joint displaced with roots and soil loss around the pipe.
Manholes at both ends of the ditch reach show heavy infiltration staining.
The ditch carries standing meltwater in spring over the cracked area.
Reaches of the same sewer under the paved road show no ground smoke.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Smoke is escaping from a natural gas line in the ditch
The ground cracks are only frost cracks with sound pipe below
The ditch reach pipe is defective at its joints and also exposed to surface inflow where meltwater ponds
Smoke travelled through gopher holes from a distant manhole

inference.explanation: Ground smoke over the pipe, a dug up displaced root filled joint, infiltration staining, and ponding over the reach fit a defective pipe taking surface water. Sound paved reaches show no smoke.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair scope best matches the findings?

options.label: Replace the entire sewer including the sound paved reaches
Repair the defective ditch reach joints and regrade the ditch so meltwater no longer ponds over the pipe
Fill the surface cracks with gravel and close the file

nextClue.explanation: Fixing both the pipe defects and the ponding addresses entry and exposure together.

clueText.nc-a: Replacing sound reaches adds cost with no defect evidence behind it.
clueText.nc-b: The scope pairs joint repairs in the ditch reach with ditch regrading, leaving the sound paved reaches in service.
clueText.nc-c: Covering cracks leaves displaced, root filled joints taking meltwater below ground.

tasks.prompt: Two neighbouring homes are suspected as dye sources in a Winnipeg street, and tests give opposite results for each.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Dye from Home A foundation drain reaches the sanitary sewer in 12 minutes on two tests.
Dye from Home B foundation drain reaches only the storm sewer on two tests.
Both homes were tested with the same crew, dye strength and observation time.
The sanitary flow response to storms is consistent with one connected drain, not two.
Home B has a sump pump that discharges to its yard, observed during testing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both homes are connected because they were built in the same year
Home B is the connected one and the dye results were mixed up
Neither home is connected and the sanitary dye was contamination
Only Home A is connected to the sanitary sewer, and only it should receive a disconnection requirement

inference.explanation: Repeated paired tests with the same method separate the two properties cleanly, and the flow response matches a single connection. Build year is not evidence of a connection.

nextClue.prompt: Which file action best reflects the paired results?

options.label: Issue requirements to both homes to be safe
Drop the file because the results differ between homes
Issue the disconnection requirement to Home A only, with both homes test records kept on file

nextClue.explanation: Acting only on the proven connection keeps the requirement defensible.

clueText.nc-a: Ordering Home B without evidence would be unfair and hard to defend.
clueText.nc-b: Differing results are the point of testing, not a reason to drop a proven case.
clueText.nc-c: The file issues the requirement to Home A and retains the negative test record for Home B.
